searchText: I just figured out that witnesses might be useful to solve this kind of issue: https://twitter.com/DeanEigenmann/status/1278027312907325443 basically, we can replace the transactions that don't touch contracts with transaction witnesses. Like, if we are watching a contract C. The block might look like: ``` transactions: [ <tx_witness_0>, <tx_witness_1>, actual_transaction_that_touches_C, <tx_witness_3>, ... ] ``` In that case we don't need to execute the transactions we aren't interested in, but we still can validate that the root hash matches. tx witnesses here should have an important property though, they should produce the state __after__ transaction execution, and not before. Which isn't really a bit deal, but will make terminology even more messy 🙂

basically, we can replace the transactions that don't touch contracts with transaction witnesses.
Like, if we are watching a contract C.
The block might look like:
```
transactions: [
     <tx_witness_0>,
     <tx_witness_1>,
     actual_transaction_that_touches_C,
     <tx_witness_3>,
     ...
]
```
In that case we don't need to execute the transactions we aren't interested in, but we still can validate that the root hash matches.
